candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: recognize serious medication adverse effects, monitor therapy, interpret relevant laboratory findings, and intervene for medication-related complications.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — SGLT2 inhibitor ketoacidosis recognition
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that SGLT2-associated DKA can present with only modest hyperglycemia and evaluate compatible symptoms for ketones and metabolic acidosis regardless of the presenting glucose level.

options.A: Diabetic ketoacidosis, because SGLT2-associated ketoacidosis can occur even when the presenting glucose is below 250 mg/dL.
options.B: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state, established solely by the glucose value of 210 mg/dL without additional testing.
options.C: Hypoglycemia, because SGLT2-related ketoacidosis requires glucose above 300 mg/dL.
options.D: Medication intolerance only; ketones and acid-base status do not need evaluation at this glucose level.

candidate.rationale: The current JARDIANCE (empagliflozin) label warns that diabetic ketoacidosis and other ketoacidosis can occur with SGLT2 inhibitors and that blood glucose at presentation may be below the levels typically expected for DKA, including below 250 mg/dL. Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, malaise, dehydration, and shortness of breath are compatible symptoms. The label directs clinicians to assess for ketoacidosis regardless of presenting blood glucose and to promptly evaluate if it is suspected. Therefore A is correct. B cannot be established from glucose 210 mg/dL, C falsely requires marked hyperglycemia for SGLT2-associated DKA, and D would inappropriately dismiss a potentially life-threatening adverse effect.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Empagliflozin-associated DKA/ketoacidosis can occur with glucose below 250 mg/dL, so compatible symptoms warrant evaluation regardless of the presenting glucose level.
candidate.source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.1: signs/symptoms include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, malaise, dyspnea; blood glucose may be below typical DKA levels (e.g., <250 mg/dL); assess for ketoacidosis regardless of presenting glucose; discontinue and promptly evaluate/treat if suspected.
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling
candidate.source_version_date: Updated February 17, 2026; prescribing information revised January 2026
candidate.stem: A client with type 2 diabetes who takes empagliflozin presents with nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, and fatigue. The blood glucose is 210 mg/dL. Which complication must still be considered?
